Source: Modified from Appendix A, Applicant's Bad Creek Environmental Report and Fishery Resource Evaluation, Mr. Don Archer, Fishery Biologist, South Carolina Wildlife and Marine Resources Department, June 1973.
A study of rainbow trout (Salmo gairdneri) in Howard Creek was conducted by Applicant biologists in April 1975 -June 1976 (Appendix K, Exhibit W) to determine growth and movements of stocked trout, reproductive success, and food habits. Reproductive success was indicated by the presence of unmarked young-of-the-year fish in electroshocked samples. Howard Creek is, therefore, presently supporting a selfsustaining rainbow trout population. Growth rates of 5.0 -7.9 mm (0.2 - 0.3 in.) per month were calculated for stocked fingerlings. Growth estimates for native young-of-the-year rainbows ranged from 7.3 - 14.7 mm per month (0.3 - 0.6 inches). Of 128 trout sampled, 10 exceeded 200 mm (about 8 inches), with the largest fish being 309 mm (12.2 inches) in length. Analyses of stomach contents showed insects to account for 97 percent of the food materials. Stoneflies constituted 69 percent of the diet by weight.
